contraindications: Uncertain if refusal to engage with thoughts may be difficult or counterproductive for individuals with severe cognitive or emotional impairments.
original_extraction.evidence_text:
Variations on this theme include ‘I can’t stand it’, ‘I can’t cope’, ‘It’s too overwhelming’, ‘I can’t
take it anymore’, ‘I’m going to have a nervous breakdown’, and so on. Your mind 1s basically
feeding you the story that you’re too weak to handle this, and something bad is going to happen if
you keep feeling this way. (And is this a helpful story to pay attention to?)

---

This is a classic! Here your mind picks an argument with reality. The reality is this: the way you are
feeling right now is the way you are feeling. But your mind says, ‘Reality is wrong! It’s not
supposed to be this way! Stop it! Give me the reality I want!” (And is this effective? Does it change
anything? Can you ever win an argument with reality?)

---

Wishful thinking: one of the mind’s favourite pastimes. (“I wish I felt more confident.’ ‘I wish I
didn’t feel so anxious.’) This can keep us wrapped up in second-guessing ourselves for hours,
imagining how our lives could be so much better if only we felt differently. (And does this help us

---

And the list could go on and on. Suffice it to say, the thinking self has lots of ways either to directly
intensify our bad feelings or else to get us to waste a huge amount of time uselessly brooding on
them. So, from now on, intend to catch your mind in the act when it tries to hook you with these
questions and comments. Then simply refuse to play the game. Thank your mind for trying to waste
your time, and focus instead on some useful or meaningful activity. You may find it helpful to say
something to yourself like, ‘Thanks, Mind, but I’m not playing today.’
generation_rules: Identify when the mind is engaging in unhelpful stories or arguments
Intend to catch the mind in the act of hooking attention
Respond by refusing to engage and redirecting focus to meaningful activity
Use self-statements such as 'Thanks, Mind, but I’m not playing today.'
pause_rules: Pause to recognize the presence of unhelpful thoughts before choosing not to engage with them.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Increasing awareness of the mind's tendency to intensify negative feelings through argument, wishful thinking, and brooding; promoting acceptance of present emotional experience without resistance.
repetition_rules: Repeatedly notice and refuse to engage with recurring unhelpful thoughts and mental arguments.
symbolic_elements: Refusing to play the mind's game
original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Interrupting unhelpful thought patterns by recognizing and refusing to engage with negative self-talk and mental arguments against reality.
voice_rules: Use a conversational, questioning tone to highlight the futility of arguing with reality
Use direct address to the mind to personify and externalize unhelpful thoughts
